reasoning: bond_fene_expand_kokkos.cpp:191-198 'if (rlogarg < 0.1) { if (rlogarg <= -3.0) d_flag() = 2; else d_flag() = 1; rlogarg = 0.1; }' -- both stores are plain, unordered writes to the same 0-d view, and the post-kernel dispatch at :133-138 is 'Kokkos::deep_copy(h_flag,d_flag); if (h_flag() == 1) error->warning(FLERR,"FENE bond too long"); else if (h_flag() == 2) error->one(FLERR,"Bad FENE bond");' -- strictly last-writer-wins, so a '1' written after a '2' downgrades a fatal condition to a warning. This is not only a thread race: even in a serial host build the bonds are processed in list order, so any later merely-too-long bond erases an earlier bad one. The CPU base raises the fatal condition per bond and cannot lose it (src/MOLECULE/bond_fene_expand.cpp:88-92 'error->warning(...); if (rlogarg <= -3.0) error->one(FLERR, "Bad FENE bond");'). bond_fene_kokkos.cpp:202-204 has the identical shape, so the fix belongs in both files.
fix: Make the severity monotone: replace the two plain stores with 'Kokkos::atomic_max(&d_flag(), 2)' and 'Kokkos::atomic_max(&d_flag(), 1)' (severity ordering 0 < 1 < 2) in both bond_fene_expand_kokkos.cpp:191-196 and bond_fene_kokkos.cpp:200-205.
